ai_view.directive: Follow as written. Prove the Revocation Linearization Law with two complementary mechanisms: an executable concurrent-state model and an independent history checker. The objective is that NO permitted ordering of concurrent operations can restore an invalid qualification as current authority after revocation commits.
ai_view.specification: Extend the in-build revocation-linearization spec (naya5/revocation-linearization) with RLQ-1: the exact safety property R_e ≺ X ∧ ¬Requalified(c,e,X) ⇒ ¬UsesRevokedProof(X,e); operations modeled with invocation/linearization-point/response (linearization point per operation type, real-time precedence respected); small abstract state (2 claims, 2 evidence, 2 publishers, 1 validator, 1 ACT, 1 recovery; Q_C=(E1∧E3)∨E2); TLA+/TLC atomic transitions (CommitRevocation/CommitQualification/CommitProjection/Validate/CommitAction/Crash/Recover/Replay) with the specification sketch; six named properties RLQ-S1..S6 (no stale certification/publication/action/rollback/replay-resurrection + independent-support preservation); crash injection at 9 sensitive points (safety holds even if every refresh worker crashes forever); recovery-as-reconciliation with the 43→41→42 adversarial order and idempotence equations; the four overlapping-operation guarantees distinguished (linearizability ≠ display freshness); 12-case adversarial matrix R1–R12 PLUS mutants (removed guards must yield counterexamples); safety vs liveness checker configurations (never assume recovery for safety); the independent history verifier (partial-order reconstruction, candidate linearizations, replay against reference machine, minimal counterexample or INCONCLUSIVE); the bounded RLQ-1 reference-model + mutation-test fixture as the smallest executable unit, independently reproduced.

decisions: Shawn's explicit framework, main chat, 2026-10-10. His word IS the verification (Verification Law).

Folded as the VERIFICATION HALF of the in-build revocation-linearization layer (dispatched ~1 min prior) — the law and its proof belong in one coherent spec. RLQ-1 is an extension of existing evidence/revocation/VERIFY contracts, not a new authority system.
intelligence.essence: Revocation Linearization Qualification (RLQ-1): prove the law with an executable concurrent-state model and an independent history checker that verifies real execution traces against that model. The decisive result is not that every refresh eventually finishes — it is that even if every cache worker crashes, messages arrive in the wrong order, and an old successor wakes up tomorrow, none of those events can restore revoked proof as current authority. Safety: no stale authority after the revocation boundary. Recovery: no rollback or resurrection despite crashes and replay. Preservation: unaffected, independently supported intelligence survives. Three things proven separately — and the model checker must also prove the negative: deliberately defective implementations (removed guards, blind replay, revision reuse, eventual-consistency reads) MUST yield counterexamples, or the specification isn't actually detecting what it claims to detect.
intelligence.falsifier: A model that passes because recovery was assumed; a mutant with the publication guard removed that yields no counterexample; a history verifier that fabricates missing commits from a success log; a liveness assumption smuggled into the safety proof; an ABA revision-reuse admitted by the checker; a display-freshness claim proven only by linearization.

human_view.meaning: Don't just trust the law — attack it. Build a miniature universe with two claims, two evidence sources, two writers racing, a revocation, and a crash-happy recovery worker, then let the machine try EVERY possible ordering of events to find a way to sneak old proof back into authority. If it can't find one, the law holds. Then comes the cruelty: deliberately break the machinery six different ways — remove the guards, let recovery blindly restore history, reuse version numbers — and the checker MUST catch each sabotage, or the test itself is worthless. Finally, take real execution traces from the actual system and verify them against the model independently. The standard isn't 'refreshes eventually finish.' It's: even if everything crashes and messages arrive backwards, revoked proof stays dead.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the verification pattern the whole stack converges on: the fairness layers got their staged model checker (SN-0771), the linearization law gets RLQ-1. The mutant requirement is the permanent innovation — a checker that can't catch deliberate sabotage proves nothing. And the safety/liveness separation is the guard against the oldest cheating in formal methods: assuming the happy path to prove the hard property. Every future law should ship with its RLQ: the machine that tries to break it.

The bounded fixture (2 evidence, 2 claims, 2 writers, 1 revocation, 1 validator, 1 action gate, 1 recovery worker) is the smallest executable unit, proven first in isolation.

naya_view.directive: Model every operation with its linearization point; respect real-time precedence. Keep the abstract state small but complete with the (E1∧E3)∨E2 support shape. Check RLQ-S1..S6 separately. Inject crashes at every sensitive point; never assume recovery for safety. Treat recovery as reconciliation with idempotence equations. Distinguish the four overlapping-operation guarantees. Prove the mutants fail. Verify real histories independently against the reference machine. Report exactly which operation boundary each property is proven at.

simple_view.meaning: Build a tiny universe, try every possible bad ordering, and prove old proof can never come back — then prove the proof itself works by breaking it on purpose.

intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor inherits the RLQ-1 pattern: every future law ships with its own adversarial model-checker and mutant suite, so verification machinery can never silently go blind.
